"REAL DRIVE

Technical Design Document (TDD)

Android Realistic Driving @COMMENT_BODY@ Learning Simulator

Document Version: 1.0
Project Status: Pre-Production / Architecture Definition
Target Platform: Android
Game Engine: Godot 4.x
Primary Language: GDScript
Secondary Tools: Blender, Git, Android SDK
Project Type: 3D Driving Simulation / Educational Driving Game
Business Model: Free-to-play prototype, with no mandatory paid dependencies

---

1. PROJECT VISION

REAL DRIVE is a realistic 3D driving and driver-training simulator designed for Android devices.

The primary objective is to create a driving experience that goes beyond conventional mobile driving games.

Unlike arcade driving games, REAL DRIVE focuses on the actual mechanical relationship between the driver, engine, clutch, transmission, wheels, brakes, and road surface.

The player must operate the vehicle rather than simply control its movement.

The game should teach and simulate:

- Starting and stopping a vehicle.
- Operating a manual transmission.
- Understanding engine RPM.
- Learning clutch engagement.
- Finding the clutch biting point.
- Changing gears correctly.
- Driving uphill and downhill.
- Reversing and parking.
- Following traffic rules.
- Handling unexpected driving situations.

The experience should combine three elements:

1. Realistic mechanical simulation.
2. Structured driving education.
3. An attractive and optimized 3D environment.

1.1 Core Design Philosophy

REAL DRIVE must prioritize:

- Mechanical consistency.
- Physically plausible vehicle behavior.
- Responsive mobile controls.
- High-quality cockpit presentation.
- Modular architecture.
- Expandability.
- Android performance.
- Educational value.

The game must not fake vehicle behavior through scripted speed changes or arbitrary acceleration animations.

Vehicle movement must emerge from the interaction of the engine, drivetrain, wheels, tires, brakes, and environment.

---

2. INITIAL PRODUCT SPECIFICATION

Property| Specification
Project name| REAL DRIVE
Platform| Android
Engine| Godot 4.x
Graphics| Real-time 3D
Camera| Cockpit only
Transmission| 5 forward + 1 reverse + neutral
Vehicle class| Iranian domestic sedan
Physics profile| Simulation
Input| Touch controls
Steering| Virtual steering wheel
Pedals| Accelerator, brake, clutch
Transmission input| Plus / Minus
Parking brake| Dedicated control
Initial environment| Driving training area
Internet requirement| None for core gameplay
Initial language| Persian
Architecture| Modular, data-driven

2.1 Initial Development Scope

The first playable version must include:

- One operational vehicle.
- One functional cockpit.
- One engine simulation.
- One manual gearbox.
- One clutch system.
- One basic suspension system.
- Functional steering.
- Functional brakes.
- Basic road contact.
- One training environment.
- Mobile user interface.
- Basic driving instructions.

The first prototype should not include a complete open-world city, multiplayer, advanced traffic simulation, or a large collection of vehicles.

These features belong to later development phases.

---

3. SYSTEM ARCHITECTURE

The project must use a modular architecture.

The physics engine must remain independent from the user interface, mission system, visual effects, and audio system.

3.1 High-Level Architecture
